# max-image-preview

*Directive*

A robots rule that sets the largest image preview Google may show for a page: none, standard or large.

**Glossary** (*max-image-preview*): A robots rule for the largest image preview Google may show: none, standard or large, for example in Discover.

Narrative: the topic [Snippets and preview controls](../topics/snippet-controls.md) tells the story; this card lists what links to it.

7 claims mention it: 5 shown or said at the event (2 confirmed by Google docs, 3 consistent with Google docs), 2 the author's analysis. A card is a map: cite the claim ids, with the citation given after each claim.

## Google's documentation

Documented in: [Robots meta tag, data-nosnippet, and X-Robots-Tag specifications](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/robots-meta-tag).

## Shown or said at the event

Not in Google's documentation first: present those as said at Search Central Live, never as documented policy.

- [`D2-C087`](../sessions/D2-S04-controlling-indexing.md) Slide, Day 2, confirmed by Google docs: The max-image-preview rule sets the maximum size of a page's image previews: none shows no preview, standard a default-sized one and large the largest possible, for example in Discover. `[D2-C087, slide, John Mueller, Day 2]`
- [`D3-C224`](../sessions/D3-S06-uncovering-trustworthy-experiences-on-discover.md) Slide, Day 3, confirmed by Google docs: Google's Discover slide recommended large images at least 1,200 px wide, with more than 300,000 total pixels and a 16x9 aspect ratio, enabled by the max-image-preview:large setting. `[D3-C224, slide, Google, Day 3]`
- [`D2-C089`](../sessions/D2-S04-controlling-indexing.md) Stage, Day 2, consistent with Google docs: max-image-preview:large matters mainly in Discover, where it allows a large image that draws people's attention, so the rule can make a page more visible than leaving it out, John Mueller said. `[D2-C089, stage, John Mueller, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C104`](../sessions/D2-S04-controlling-indexing.md) Slide, Day 2, consistent with Google docs: To be as visible as possible in Google, John Mueller's closing slide recommended the robots rules max-image-preview:large and max-snippet:-1. `[D2-C104, slide, John Mueller, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C936`](../sessions/D2-S13-using-images-to-your-advantage-and-engaging-search-users-with-videos.md) Stage, Day 2, consistent with Google docs: Setting the max-image-preview robots meta tag to large can make content perform surprisingly well in Discover, Gary Illyes said. `[D2-C936, stage, Gary Illyes, Day 2]`

## The author's analysis

- [`D2-C105`](../sessions/D2-S04-controlling-indexing.md) Analysis: Set max-snippet:-1 and max-image-preview:large on every indexable template unless licensing requires otherwise, and check that no CMS, plug-in or CDN setting adds lower snippet or image preview limits by default. `[D2-C105, analysis, Ibrahim Anjro]`
- [`D3-C230`](../sessions/D3-S06-uncovering-trustworthy-experiences-on-discover.md) Analysis: For Discover, set max-image-preview:large on article templates, give every article a relevant image at least 1,200 px wide in og:image or schema.org markup that is neither the site logo nor text-heavy, and show clear bylines and dates. `[D3-C230, analysis, Ibrahim Anjro]`

## For developers

- `DEV-IDX-04` **SHOULD** · Documented: Allow full snippets and large previews with max-snippet:-1 and max-image-preview:large (5 of its claims mention it; its own text names it)
- `DEV-IMG-07` **SHOULD** · Documented: Give every article a large, relevant lead image and declare it in og:image or markup (2 of its claims mention it; its own text names it)
